newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks dip, no recovery in sight.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks dip, no recovery in sight.

text.p: Croatian stocks took another dip on Friday, ending a poorly traded week with no recovery in sight.
"The situation is not likely to change significantly next week," one market watcher said.
"We keep saying prices are so low that they are bound to rise but it yet remains to be seen," she said.
Five of 10 traded issues fell, only one rose and four were flat. Volume dwindled to 1,182 units, turnover to 0.8 million kuna -- lowest in months.
An absence of big buyers this week deepened losses almost across the board.
Blue chip Pliva pharmaceuticals was the day's only gainer, adding 10 kuna to 460. With 275 shares sold it was also the most actively traded issue.
Pliva was among the few issues that recouped part of their recent losses, closing 35 kuna stronger than a week ago.
The other top bracket issue, Zagrebacka Banka ordinary stock, edged down 0.10 kuna to 1,850 with 220 units sold. It also recovered from last Friday's close of 1,820 kuna.
Food stock Podravka, falling six kuna or 1.5 percent to 289 kuna on volume of 132 shares, led the day's decliners. It ended this week 12 kuna lower than last Friday.
Other decliners included hotelier Riviera Porec, Adriatic pipeline operator Janaf and Zagrebacka C-series bearer stock.
Confectioner Kras, hotel stock Jadranturist, textile firm Varteks and Zagrebacka Banka's preferred shares were unchanged from Thursday.
